title: What You Were Given and What You Pass On
excerpt: A hard truth, a legacy, a faith passed down and ten healed men. This week asked what we pass on, and whether we remember what we were given.

seo_description: Four Scriptures, three insights, two questions and one action step on leaving a legacy, speaking up, the faith passed down to you and giving thanks.
body_html: What You Were Given and What You Pass On
What a hard truth, a legacy, a letter from Christ, a grandmother’s faith and ten healed men taught us this week

This week we looked at what gets passed on. A team that sees the problem but won’t say it. A family that keeps the habits but loses the story. A leader whose choices keep forming people after he’s gone. A faith that lived first in a grandmother and a mother. And ten healed men, only one of whom came back.
The leadership series ended Wednesday. Thanksgiving began Thursday. But it was one thread. This week was about leaving a legacy, and about thanking God for the one you were given.
Before asking what you will leave behind, consider what you received.

One-Minute Win of the Week
Before your Thanksgiving meal, take 60 seconds and name one person who passed faith to you. Then send them a text that says thank you.

A father sits at the Thanksgiving table. He passed on the rules and the routines. Church on Sunday. Grace before dinner. Work hard. Don’t quit. His kids know them all. But they’ve never heard the night he almost walked away. The prayer God answered. The mercy that met him. This year, before the plates go around, he tells them. Same table. Same habits. But now the next generation knows where to put its trust.
“We will not hide them from their descendants; we will tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the LORD, his power, and the wonders he has done.”
Insight: The purpose of telling the story is formation, not nostalgia: the next generation must learn where to place its trust.
Gem: Infrastructure can be inherited. Conviction has to be taught.

“You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone. You show that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.”
Insight: The letter is from Christ and written by the Spirit, and that keeps the leader from becoming the center of transformation.
Gem: We are stewards of what we build, not owners of the people it forms.
“I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, now lives in you also.”
Insight: Timothy’s faith didn’t come from a program or a platform. It came from two women with names.
Gem: Some of the greatest gifts we carry came through people who expected nothing in return.
“One of them, when he saw he was healed, came back, praising God in a loud voice. He threw himself at Jesus’ feet and thanked him—and he was a Samaritan.”
Insight: All ten were healed, but only the one who came back heard, “Your faith has made you well.”
Gem: Gratitude doesn’t just acknowledge the gift. It brings us back to the Giver.
• Silence is not agreement. Silence in the meeting may be evidence that people have learned what happens when they speak.
• Legacy is what keeps forming. The work we complete and the people we form are not always the same measure of success.
• Familiarity makes grace invisible. Much of what we now call normal was once something we hoped and prayed for.
• What would continue if I disappeared tomorrow?
• What blessing has become so familiar that I barely notice it?

Write three names: Write down three people whose influence shaped your life. Next to each name, write what they gave you. Thank them if you can. A text, a call, a note. If they are no longer living, thank God for them. Then ask how you might pass that gift forward.
The leadership series ended where it began. Systems don’t begin in a vacuum. They begin in people:
• People who never met the original leader
What begins inside people can eventually become the environment that shapes other people. That’s the battle before the battle. It still starts in your heart.
Want to trace it upstream in your own life? Walk through the Upstream Formation Framework.
Gem: Your organization may keep teaching long after you stop speaking.

Prayer
Father, thank You for every person You used to shape my life. Open my eyes to the gifts I have stopped noticing. Make me teachable. Give me a heart that prepares others. Teach me to steward faithfully, develop generously, and release humbly. May the next generation know You, not merely know what we built. Teach me to turn around and come back with thanksgiving. In Jesus’ name, amen.

Declaration
I will remember what I was given. I will pass on what was good, and point the next man to Christ.

Challenge: Thanksgiving is Thursday. Before you eat, tell someone at your table one thing God has done for you. Your kids, your wife, a younger man. Say it out loud. Then look for one chance to say thank you to another person.
Invitation: If this hit you where you are, share it with a friend. Let’s build men of faith, together.
